reviews.summary: Three fixes: use the {free:bouquet} token instead of a typed 'Premium, paid once'; the 7 gift rule FAQ listed 'something to do' as an extra, contradicting the body; 'one of the most searched questions' was an unsupported ranking claim.

Every Ethos claim checked out. Fixes: the 'book or film' row mentioned margins and chapter four, so book only; Spanish FAQ 'aprendida por ella' read as 'learned by her'; 'regalo detallista' describes a person, not a gift, in Spain; 'un regalo del que se va a enterar' read as a threat.

Nothing has to change: against The Knot's stage-sorted list and the engraved-product listicles it adds a written line for each stage, an hour-tonight and week-long plan, a way to mine her messages for what she wants, and answers to every People also ask question.

applied: Bouquet card uses {free:bouquet} in both languages

'one of the most searched questions' replaced with 'People ask this a lot' (ES likewise)
Spanish FAQ wording: 'aprendida para ella', 'algo que hayas aprendido por ella', 'regalo con detalle', 'se lo van a contar'
Polish: 'four short letters in envelopes', 'fotos después', 'por ejemplo, una carta como', '¿También buscas algo para él/ella?'
rejected: Polish not taken: a Gen Z line (variant PAA only), moving the tonight section up, US spellings (the blog's house style is British spelling), a long-distance line; not needed and would add unreviewed text

reviews.summary: All round-one reader fixes made; it beats the list-style top results because every idea comes with a line only she could be given.
Round-one fixes all made. Remaining: the 7 gift rule FAQ (EN and ES) described 4 + 3 while the body says 5 + 2; the Spanish takeaway 'Ese es el tipo sentimental' read as 'the sentimental guy'.
It covers every idea the product roundups lead with and adds a stage table with lines to write, time-based plans and direct answers to each People also ask question none of them give.

reviews.summary: It is the page I'd send a friend because nearly every idea carries a line she could copy tonight and a way to find the gift in her own messages, where rival lists just name engravable objects.
Unlike the engraving-led lists, it sorts ideas by how long you've been together and how much time you have and gives each a specific line to write, in two languages that are both accurate.
It's the page to send a friend over the product lists because it tells the reader what to write, not just what to buy, and answers every main-keyword People also ask question.
